main_text.p: Diphthongi quoque propriæ, aliæ sunt mutabiles, aliæ immutabiles.II.
Mutabiles sunt; au, au, & oi. Namque au mutari solet in η:αω in ηυ: οι in ω.
Immutabiles sunt, ει, ου, υ. [Quanquam Attici ου quoque in ηυ mutare solent.]
main_text.head: De Consonantibus.
main_text.p: I.Consonantes sunt septendecim: Mutæ novem; Semivocales octo.
II.Mutæ, in tres ordines, sibi invicem respondentes, tribuuntur. Aliæ namque sunt,
I.Semivocales, liquidæ sunt quatuor; λ, μ, ν, ρ: illiquida simplex una; σ: duplices tres; ζ, ξ, ψ.
III.[Observatio 1. Litera γ, ante aliud γ, vel ante κ, ξ, χ, positum, euphoniæ causâ effertur ut ν. ut: ἄγγελος, ἄγκυρα, λύγξ, ἔλεγχος.
2. Litera ν, mutatur in μ, ante β, μ, π, φ, ψ: in γ, ante γ, κ, χ: in λ, ρ, σ, ante eadem has literas positum.]

page.notes: Signature "A 3" at foot; catchword "De" at lower right. Greek words in the observatio are printed in Greek letters as best read. Marginal numerals I, II, III are side notes marking paragraphs.
